data.body:
AC4 (local detector) IMPLEMENTED and independently verified on this host. AC2 patch written but NOT applied -- awaiting operator decision, since the target is a machine-local script.

THE DETECTOR REPORTS THE REAL BUG. Verified by me directly, not taken on report:
  doctor: build freshness
    [error] reject-streak: the main-tracking updater has rejected 122 consecutive candidates (threshold 3) ...
    [error] build-stale: the published rebar build (cdfd7d94d, 2026-08-29) is 201 commit(s) behind origin/main (6125c5345), over the 25-commit threshold -- gate results from it can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show
Note the numbers MOVED between the implementer's run and mine: streak 121 -> 122, drift 200 -> 201. The stall is ongoing and worsening hourly, which is itself corroboration.

SHAPE: a scan module inside the existing 'rebar doctor' command, NOT a new scripts/check_*.py. The check_orphaned_load.py precedent was weighed and SPLIT rather than copied: its ON-DEMAND half is exactly right (live host state is not a property of the tree under review, so it does not belong in make lint), but its LOCATION is not -- scripts/ is where this repo puts things that gate or report on the TREE. doctor_mcp_client.py is the closer structural match: it reads the operator's home directory, degrades every fault to a finding, renders its own section, and stays advisory outside the exit code and outside --repair. That contract was copied exactly, plus a has_blocking_build_freshness() seam for a caller that does want to gate. AC4 also names a 'rebar' invocation as its first example. Secondary argument, and a good one: an operator already runs 'rebar doctor', whereas a script nobody knows exists is a detector with the same silence problem as the dead SNS topic.

TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS, deliberately not one: reject-streak catches an updater that is FAILING; build-stale (>25 commits behind) catches one that STOPPED RUNNING, and survives a hand-reset counter. Threshold justified from data rather than picked: a healthy hourly updater sits 0-2 commits behind, and the two recorded incidents were ~48 and ~195, so 25 is below the smaller incident and an order of magnitude above healthy.

REUSE, NOT REIMPLEMENTATION: the commit-distance walk is build_drift.detect_drift, extended with one keyword-only build_sha parameter defaulting to running_build_sha(). It previously read only the RUNNING process's sha, which cannot answer 'how stale is the build the updater published' from a dev checkout. All existing callers unchanged.

NO NEW MECHANISM. _detect_gate_scripts was checked BEFORE designing (it names a ci_gate by the repo-relative path of any scripts/check_*.py), which is precisely why the detector is not one. check_mechanism_delta.py --check reports new=0, and test_mechanism_delta.py passes 31/31. No marker, no baseline edit.

A GATE CAUGHT A DESIGN FICTION, worth recording as a positive: the first draft read XDG_STATE_HOME, which check_config_ownership.py rejected as an 'unresolved-env-read below approved seam'. Rather than add a marker to keep it, the env read was REMOVED -- because the updater itself does not consult XDG_STATE_HOME (its default is ${HOME}/.local/state/rebar-dev), so honoring it described a layout that is never written. The module now reads no environment at all. The gate did not just block a violation; it surfaced that the code was accommodating something fictional. Documented limitation: an operator who relocated state via the updater's own REBAR_DEV_STATE_DIR passes state_dir= to the scan.

Verification: make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (755 files); test_mechanism_delta.py 31 passed; 110 targeted passed; 102 regression passed. RED first: ImportError for the absent module, then 14 passed.

AC2 PATCH READY BUT UNAPPLIED. Live ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh confirmed byte-identical to its original. It honors the operator's direction -- no pinned local tool, and no substituted absolute path: UV_BIN's hardcoded default is removed, REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only as a HINT that is validated like any other candidate rather than trusted, and the pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml AFTER checkout (the earliest point it exists, and why the value tracks main rather than this host). Every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact match wins, so PATH ORDER STOPS BEING LOAD-BEARING in either direction. Exact string comparison suffices without a version solver because check_uv_pin.py contractually guarantees an exact ==X.Y.Z and fails the build on a range; any other shape is refused loudly rather than guessed.

Exercised against the real host (functions extracted to a harness; the updater itself never run):
  real pyproject ==0.12.7  -> selects ~/.local/bin/uv, THE BINARY THE CURRENT HARDCODE EXCLUDES
  unsatisfiable ==9.9.9    -> names required version, every version found, and every path inspected
  wrong hint (0.12.9)      -> rejected, correct 0.12.7 chosen (validated, not trusted)
  range pin / no pin       -> refused loudly
Failures now reject at a new 'uv-select' stage, so the log and reject-streak name binary selection rather than blaming sync.

AC1 depends on AC2 being applied (operator's call). AC3 was rescoped away by the operator. AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' and the 5fb69334...1559 partial-release stub) remains open and untouched.

AC2 HAS NO REPO-SIDE TEST and cannot have one: the script is machine-local and git-ignored, so nothing in the tree can reach it. The evidence is the harness run above.
